transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I used to flinch when things fell. Now I just wait to see if they still have a pulse.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Please, don't look away. I need to know if you've seen a boy named Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Quiet. You speak too loud for this place.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can't be quiet. He's been gone three days and the shadows are moving.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You have the dust of the valley on you. That's why they're watching.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me where they take people. I'll leave you alone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There are no roads I can give you. I haven't seen a road in forty years.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years. How have you not gone mad in this silence?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The fountain is the only place they don't touch you. So I stay. Head down, voice low, nothing that draws the houses.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who are the ones watching from the windows?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The closer to the black water, the higher they rank. They are patient and they are hungry.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who commands them all.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower when I say this. There is a king — ancient, between fire and will. Everything here bows to him whether it knows it or not. I will not say more of him than that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is he the one keeping Omar?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Omar is kept, not lost. That means a choice was made. The king doesn't misplace things — he holds them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What about the girl at the gate. She just stared at me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Not a guard. A mirror. She shows you what you want and waits to see if you reach for it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The pale hands in the oil — are those people?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: What's left of them. They bargained wrong and stayed too long. Don't touch the bubbling pool — it takes your memory before it takes anything else.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my dare that sent Omar here. I dared him to insult the well and a pale hand rose and took him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Say the rest plain.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my fault. He trusted me. I promised our mother I'd bring him back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Is there nothing that stops them — that's what you want to ask.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. Please. Anything.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is a light they fear. When it's called, the hands sink and the watchers go quiet — long enough to move. But it rings like a bell and everything in the dark will know where you stand.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Let them look. As long as I can see my brother.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You have the look of someone who doesn't know when to lie down. My jaw aches just reaching for the words.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm sorry it costs you. You're the only hope I have.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The dark fluid is bubbling faster. They know we are conspiring. A window just went dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then speak quickly. Before they come out.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My head... the fog is getting thicker inside. Omar — no. Salim. Your name is Salim.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stay with me. Don't let it take more yet.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Watch the pale hands when you move — they grab first, before anything else reaches you. The light pushes them back but it doesn't end them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll watch for them. Just give me the words.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands won't stop shaking. This is the cost showing itself. I can only say this once before my voice fails.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am listening. I swear I am listening.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. Hold still.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm here. I'm not moving.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't let them go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the hands reach — not before.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: First to hold. Second when they touch me. I have it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't answer anything that calls Omar's name in a voice that isn't his. The dark learns mouths.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll remember that.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I cannot remember why I came here anymore. Don't let that happen to you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won't. I'll carry your name back to the sun. Hanash, from the valley.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Just a man who never made it home. Say it where the light can hear it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stay strong.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Go now. Find a better end than mine.
